7cf7b9b Draw wide tables as text and delete the wide-table overlay
A table wider than its column was hosted in an NSScrollView holding an
NSImageView with a rasterized copy of it, one per table. That is where
the memory went: 13 of the SOP's 15 tables are wide, and each of them
cost a bitmap plus CoreAnimation's copy of that bitmap, whether or not it
was on screen. The overlay existed because TextKit 2 caches a rendering
surface per layout fragment, which defeated scrolling inside one.

The fragment now draws a wide table like a narrow one — from its measured
layout, clipped to the column and shifted by an offset kept per table —
with a drawn scroller along the bottom. Nothing is rasterized any more.

What made that possible is the answer to the surface-cache question:
TextKit 2 gives every layout fragment its own layer-backed subview and
renders the fragment into that view's backing store. No public
invalidation reaches it once the fragment exists —
invalidateRenderingAttributes, invalidateLayout on the manager or on the
fragment, and layoutViewport all leave the fragment object standing, and
a standing fragment keeps its surface. Invalidating the view under the
table's box does repaint it, at 0.065 ms a step and 114 repaints in 114
steps. That is the one place in the engine that depends on the view
structure; it depends on geometry alone, names no class, degrades to a
table that stops repainting rather than to a crash, and has a tripwire
test with a real window and the real viewport machinery.

Also here, because wide tables are unusable without it: the tables are
re-measured when the reading column changes width. A table's column
widths are fixed at the width it was styled at, and with a reading column
nothing re-measured them — the editor is styled at a provisional 925 pt
and the column then settles at 736 pt, which left the table spilling out
of the column it was drawn in. That is the width error from step 3.

Measured on the Mini, sop.md, Release, three rounds, median footprint at
rest: 372 MB with the overlay (build 2026-09-06-022), 66 MB with the same
binary rasterizing but not hosting (PTYPE_TABLE_BITMAPS=1), 58 MB on the
text path. vmmap shows no CG raster data category at all on the text
path, against 75.5 MB resident with the overlay.

Engine suite 538 tests; the two ScrollingHeaderControllerTests animation
tests are the pair that is flaky on this machine and fails at 346392c too.

6a6a12e Reconcile the wide-table overlays once after a staged open, and restyle the head's tables for the settled width
Every chunk restyle scheduled the overlay reconcile, and each pass against the
estimated geometry of that phase left rendered layers behind: a 441-kB document
with wide tables sat at 198 MiB after opening on the Mini (Debug) against 42 MiB
without those passes. The restyle now skips the reconcile while the staged open
runs and the finish reconciles once against the exact layout.

The finish also restyles the table paragraphs when the text container changed
width since the head was styled. SwiftUI hands the first update pass a
provisional width (925 pt for an 800-pt window), the reading column settles
afterwards, and with a reading column a width change restyles no tables; the
chunks rendered their tables for the real width while the head kept the wrong
one. The styler's Debug note now names the width it rendered for and how many
tables it marked as wider than the column.

00b4ef7 Open a large document in stages: style the head, then chunks in the background
Opening styled every paragraph and laid the whole document out twice before the
first frame. Now the rebuild styles the first block-aligned ~24k characters and
queues the rest as ~32k chunks; each runloop turn styles one chunk and lays the
document out up to its end, keeps the line at the top of the viewport anchored
by the change in fragment heights above it, and raises an extrapolated height
floor so the scroller and caret reveals reach text the layout has not got to.
Scrolling into unstyled text pulls the chunks under the viewport forward; edits
move the pending ranges along (untrusted edits re-plan from the edit); a saved
scroll offset drains the queue first; find highlights survive a chunk restyle;
the tail carries its wiki-link ids from the start; the exact height is measured
once at the end. The open-path recalcOverscroll calls measure the estimate
("open" tag) instead of forcing a full layout, and the plain-text full layout in
makeNSView is gone. Debug-only PerfTrace frames break the rebuild and each turn
down.

    private let source = "# Alpha\n\nAlpha body one.\n\n## Beta\n\nBeta body.\n\n# Gamma\n\nGamma body.\n"

    private func sections(for source: String) -> [FoldSection] {

        return FoldSection.make(from: index, map: SourceDisplayMap(engineDocumentId: "t", revision: 0, source: source))

        let alpha = sections[0], beta = sections[1], gamma = sections[2]
        let gammaStart = range(of: "# Gamma", in: source).location
        XCTAssertEqual(alpha.headingLocation, 0)
        XCTAssertEqual(alpha.hidden, NSRange(location: ("# Alpha\n" as NSString).length, length: gammaStart - ("# Alpha\n" as NSString).length))
        XCTAssertEqual(beta.hidden.location, NSMaxRange(range(of: "## Beta\n", in: source)))
        XCTAssertEqual(NSMaxRange(beta.hidden), gammaStart)
        XCTAssertTrue(gamma.canFold)
        XCTAssertEqual(NSMaxRange(gamma.hidden), (source as NSString).length)
        XCTAssertFalse(self.sections(for: "# Only\n").first!.canFold)
        // The caret on the heading line, in the body, and at the document end all belong to a section.
        let length = (source as NSString).length
        XCTAssertEqual(sections.innermost(containing: 3, documentLength: length)?.title, "Alpha")
        XCTAssertEqual(sections.innermost(containing: range(of: "Beta body", in: source).location, documentLength: length)?.title, "Beta")
        XCTAssertEqual(sections.innermost(containing: length, documentLength: length)?.title, "Gamma")
        XCTAssertEqual(sections.enclosing(range(of: "Beta body", in: source).location, documentLength: length).map(\.title), ["Alpha", "Beta"])
    }

    /// Applies the edit to the text the way the storage reports it, then runs both checks.
    private func edit(_ model: inout FoldModel, _ text: inout String, replacing range: NSRange, with replacement: String) -> Int {
        text = (text as NSString).replacingCharacters(in: range, with: replacement)
        let dropped = model.textDidChange(replacing: range, insertedLength: (replacement as NSString).length)
        return dropped.count + model.dropFoldsWithBrokenLines(in: text as NSString).count

    func testFoldsShiftWithEditsAroundThemAndExpandWhenTouched() {
        let sections = self.sections(for: source)
        var model = FoldModel()
        model.fold(sections[1])
        let beta = model.folds[0]
        var text = source

        touched = model
        touchedText = text
        XCTAssertEqual(edit(&touched, &touchedText, replacing: NSRange(location: beta.headingLocation - 2, length: 2), with: ""), 1)

# Session Crosslink

## Response Format

Begin the first response to this skill invocation with the line:

`Entire Session Crosslink:`

followed by a blank line, then the content. Apply the header to the **first response of the invocation only** — not on follow-up turns and not on error / early-exit responses (no session resolved, no affected repos found).

## STOP — Read these rules before doing ANYTHING

1. **Do NOT ask clarifying questions until the resolver/discovery steps have run.** The session id and candidate repo list usually resolve from `entire session current --json` plus what the user said. Only ask if both come back empty.
2. **Do NOT run `entire session attach` without showing the preview table first.** The whole point of this skill is preview-then-confirm. `attach` amends the target repo's HEAD; previewing wrong means amending the wrong commit.
3. **Always `cd` into the target repo before running `entire session attach`.** The CLI resolves the repo from cwd. Use one `cd … && entire session attach …` per call so each invocation hits the right repo.

Required CLI: `entire` 0.6.2+. No special flags needed — this skill works against the shipped CLI via cwd-scoped `entire session attach`.

## Flow

### Step 1: Resolve the session id

Try each strategy in order until one returns a session id.

**Strategy A: Entire-enabled cwd.**

```bash
entire session current --json
```

If the output is valid JSON **and** has a non-empty `session_id`, read `session_id` and `agent` and continue with those values. If the JSON parses but `session_id` is missing or empty, treat Strategy A as failed and fall through to B — don't proceed to attach with no session id.

**Strategy B: Entire-enabled sibling repo.** If the user named a repo that has Entire enabled (e.g. `the foo repo`), `cd` there and re-try `entire session current --json`. The session state lives wherever the session was tracked.

**Strategy C: Runtime-specific transcript directory.** If neither A nor B works, the session was never recorded by Entire and you must read it from the agent runtime:

- **Claude Code:** transcripts live at `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl`. Encoded cwd is the launch directory with `/` → `-`. The most recent `.jsonl` file under the project directory matching the agent's launch cwd is this session. Read the basename minus `.jsonl` as `session_id`. Set `agent` to `claude-code`.
- **Codex:** check `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/` or `~/.codex/sessions/`. Set `agent` to `codex`.
- **Other runtimes:** ask the user for the session id.

Record `agent` so Step 4 can pass `--agent <name>` to attach.

**If all strategies fail:** print "Could not resolve a session id — pass one explicitly or run from an Entire-enabled directory" and stop.

### Step 2: Discover affected repos

Build a candidate set, union from these sources, then de-duplicate by path:

1. **From the user's message**: any repo paths or aliases the user named explicitly (e.g. "the foo repo and the bar api"). Resolve aliases via the user's `CLAUDE.md` or treat as filesystem paths.

2. **From sibling repos under the launch directory** (only if launch dir is NOT Entire-enabled): list immediate subdirectories that have their own `.git` and a `.entire/settings.json`.

3. **From the agent's edit history in this session**: any repo whose files were edited during the session — derive from the agent's own context. If unsure, ask the user.

For each candidate, run `entire status --json` (with cwd inside that repo) and decide:

- `"enabled": true` → keep.
- `"enabled": false` with a settings-parse error (`unknown field "..."`) → keep. Status fails noisily on misconfigured local settings even when attach would succeed.
- `"enabled": false` with no error → drop. Repo opted out of Entire.

If the candidate set is empty, ask the user which repos to crosslink.

### Step 3: Compute the preview locally

For each candidate, inspect git and the session store to compute the action — same logic `entire session attach` uses internally, but without amending anything:

```bash
# Get HEAD hash and message
HEAD_HASH=$(git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD)
HEAD_MSG=$(git -C <repo> log -1 --format=%B HEAD)

# Existing Entire-Checkpoint trailer on HEAD, if any
EXISTING_TRAILER=$(printf '%s\n' "$HEAD_MSG" | grep -E '^Entire-Checkpoint:' | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}')

# Is the session already tracked in this repo's store?
STATE_FILE=<repo>/.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json
```

Decide the action per repo:

- Both `STATE_FILE` exists AND its `last_checkpoint_id` field is non-empty → `would_skip_existing_in_state`. Attach is a no-op; report that.
- HEAD has an `EXISTING_TRAILER` → `would_link_existing_in_head`. Attach reuses that checkpoint id and adds this session to it.
- Neither → `would_add_trailer`. Attach generates a fresh checkpoint id and amends HEAD with it.

For `would_link_existing_in_head` rows, the checkpoint id is `EXISTING_TRAILER`. For `would_add_trailer` rows, the checkpoint id can't be known ahead of time — attach generates one at write time. Show "new" in the table.

If HEAD has no commits in the repo (`git rev-parse` fails), record an error row: `error: no commits yet`.

### Step 4: Render the preview table

Show the user a compact table:

```
repo                              HEAD commit   action                          checkpoint
foo                               a1b2c3d       would_add_trailer               (new)
bar                               e4f5g6h       would_link_existing_in_head     ckpt-7d6c
baz                               —             error: no commits yet           —
```

Then ask: "Attach session `<id>` to the would_* rows? Error rows and `would_skip_existing_in_state` rows will be skipped."

### Step 5: Execute on confirmation

For each row the user confirmed where `action` is `would_add_trailer` or `would_link_existing_in_head`:

```bash
cd <repo> && entire session attach <session-id> --agent <agent> --force
```

Skip `would_skip_existing_in_state` rows (re-attach there is a no-op) and `error:` rows.

Capture exit status per repo. Report a final summary:

```
attached:
  foo    ckpt-9f8e  (new trailer on a1b2c3d)
  bar    ckpt-7d6c  (added to existing checkpoint on e4f5g6h)
skipped:
  baz    (no commits yet)
  qux    (already linked: ckpt-c97b)
```

Remind the user: attach amends HEAD, so each touched repo's local branch has diverged from its remote. If those branches have open PRs, force-push (`git push --force-with-lease`) to update them.

## Failure modes

- **Session id not resolvable**: stop with a one-line message — see Step 1.
- **No candidate repos**: ask the user which repos to crosslink.
- **All candidates report `would_skip_existing_in_state`**: tell the user the session is already linked everywhere; no work to do.
- **A repo's `attach` fails mid-run after others succeeded**: do not retry automatically. Report which repos succeeded vs failed and surface the failing repo's stderr. The succeeded amends are idempotent — re-running the skill is safe.
- **HEAD has no commits in a candidate**: skip that row with `error: no commits yet`. Tell the user to make at least one commit there first.
- **`entire session attach` fails with `Entire is disabled`**: the target repo opted out. Tell the user; don't retry.

## Why this skill exists

Entire tracks agent sessions per repo via state stored under each repo's git common dir. When an agent runs from a higher-level folder, a sibling repo, or a non-Entire-enabled parent, none of the child repos see the session. This skill resolves the session id from the agent runtime (which always has it), discovers affected repos, previews each, then runs `entire session attach` per repo on confirmation — without amending the wrong commit or asking the user to babysit per-repo `cd`s.

Führe genau EINEN kurzen gezielten GUI-Retest des ausdrücklich von Patrick beauftragten ptype-Scroll-Bugfixes aus. Kontext: ⌘↓ erreichte logisches Dateiende, Layout ließ Inhalt/Scrollgriff aber zurückspringen. Main hat Runtime-Slot freigegeben; keine alten Performance-Aufträge, keine Größenserie, keine Subagents oder neuen Tasks. Arbeitsordner /Users/patrick/ptype-qa-20260914-scroll; eigener unveränderlicher App-Pfad /Users/patrick/ptype-qa-20260914-scroll/ptype.app. Erwarteter Executable-SHA256 e01bec7be7710ff831bea200e4fbaa3602e4c77aee0822da40788e255cc3f419. original.md enthält 500 wiederholte Markdown-Abschnitte und eindeutigen Endmarker UNIQUE-DOCUMENT-END mit abschließender Leerzeile. original.md bleibt unverändert, erstelle regression.md als eigene Kopie.

Keine Konfigurations-, Rechte-, Trust-, TCC-, Serviceänderungen oder Installation. HOME/CODEX_HOME und vorhandene MCP unverändert. Keine alte Session resumieren. Python nur über uv. Beachte governing AGENTS und lies /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/cua_node/lib/node_modules/@oai/sky/docs/skills/oai_sky_lib/macos/SKILL.md. Prüfe vor Start Kollisionen mit eigener exakt gleicher App-Kopie und lasse fremde Instanzen/Fenster unberührt. Normales open -n mit eigenem App-Pfad und regression.md. Prüfe Codesign, Exe-SHA, eigene PID/Executablepfad und DokumentURL vor Eingaben. Bei fremdem Dokument/Fenster, sichtbarem Nutzereingriff oder unklarer Identität keine weiteren Eingaben; eigenes normales Cleanup und Abweichung melden.

Ablauf mit echten Tastatur-/Mausaktionen, keine Dateiersetzung:
1. Eigenes Dokument fokussieren. ⌘↑, dann Q, Save. Ganze Bytes müssen exakt b'Q'+original sein. Undo, Save -> original; Redo, Save -> Q+original. Damit ist die kleine Editsequenz abgeschlossen.

3. ⌘↑ und sichtbarer Dokumentanfang belegen. Rechten Scrollgriff durch echten öffentlichen drag/drag_from_to mit aus frischem Screenshot abgeleiteten Koordinaten bis ans untere Ende ziehen. 4. Final Undo, Save -> original Bytes (Navigation/Scrollen dürfen Undo nicht ersetzen). Normales Quit nur eigener Appinstanz. Prozesskontrolle nach Quit ohne Sky-get-state: PID weg, Exe-SHA unverändert, Codesign gültig, Datei exakt original. Kein ForceQuit/SIGKILL.
